course_name_original: Fundamentos físicos de la ingeniería ii
prerequisites: FUNDAMENTOS FÍSICOS DE LA INGENIERÍA I/20224004

learning_outcomes.text: Applies correctly the basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism for solving engineering problems.
Verifies through experimentation and group work in the laboratory the theoretical foundations explained in the classroom.

Understands the theory of Newtonian mechanics. Applies vector calculus concepts to solve problems in Newtonian mechanics and rigid body dynamics. Knows the fundamentals of electrical and magnetic phenomena. Solves problems of DC and AC circuits. Relates electric and magnetic fields. Knows the principles of wave theory. Identifies the theoretical foundations applied to problem solving.
Facilitates the positive management of differences, disagreements, and conflicts that arise in the team.

Considers the viewpoints of others and provides constructive feedback. Identifies the group's collective objectives with their own. Contributes to the establishment and application of team work processes. Contributes to group cohesion through their communication and interpersonal skills.

Participates actively and shares information, knowledge, and experiences. Carries out their individual contribution within the planned time and with available resources. Accepts and adheres to group norms. Collaborates actively in team work planning, task distribution, and required deadlines.

syllabus_topics: Equations defining the rotation of a rigid body around an axis
Absolute velocity and relative velocity in plane motion
Instantaneous center of rotation in plane motion
Absolute and relative acceleration in plane motion
Time derivative of a vector with respect to a rotating reference frame
Plane motion of a particle with respect to a rotating reference frame
Plane motion of a rigid body, forces and accelerations
Equations of motion of a rigid body
Angular momentum of a rigid body in plane motion
Plane motion of a rigid body
Plane motion of a rigid body; Energy and momentum methods
Work of forces applied to a rigid body
Kinetic energy of a rigid body in plane motion
Impulse-momentum theorem in plane motion of a rigid body
Ideal gases and equation of state
assessment_rules: It is an essential but not sufficient condition to pass the course to have completed and approved the laboratory practices. In the 2nd sitting, the laboratory grade (20%) will be maintained, and a written exam covering all course topics (80%) will be administered.
